## CI differential: the fix is confirmed in the environment that exhibited the defect

The completion gate's open question was trigger attribution — the crash was never reproduced
on 3.11, so nothing tied the fix to the failure it claims to repair. That evidence now exists,
produced by CI rather than locally.

Gerrit change 3008 (ticket `2277-7043-1f63-4f5c`) is an unrelated change to the Jira DC
harness. Its two patchsets form a clean differential, because CI checks out the exact patchset
with no rebase step, so each patchset's parent is the code it actually ran against:

| Arm | Parent | py3.11 gating result |
|---|---|---|
| ps1 — **without** this fix | pre-fix main | **crashed** — `test_worker_cancellation_survives_job_completion_race`, 20443 passed |
| ps2 — **with** this fix | `641531e62e5` (this fix merged) | **passed** — 20479 passed, no opcert failure |

Only the parent differs between the arms. The change's own diff is identical across both and
touches nothing on the opcert path. The failing test named in ps1 is the exact test this
ticket's fix targets.

## Relation to the null local experiment

This supersedes the local differential recorded earlier, and explains it rather than
contradicting it. That experiment was **0 reproductions in 140 attempts** on a real 3.11.16
venv under xdist, with the pre-fix arm passing 40/40 — a control proving the local harness had
no discriminating power for this defect, which is why the post-fix arm's 40/40 was reported as
meaningless on its own rather than as confidence.

The defect needs CI's scheduling to surface. CI is therefore the only instrument that could
attribute it, and it has now done so in both directions: the failure present without the fix,
absent with it.

Unverified: nothing further on this path. ps2 is red on a different, unrelated test-scaffolding
defect (`4a6f-0fd8-a04a-4e95`), which does not bear on this attribution.
